sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento delle tensioni geopolitiche in Medio Oriente e dell'incertezza economica globale. Il VIX è a 19.11, in calo del 1.04%, ma ancora sopra la soglia di 18. L'S&P 500 è sceso dello 0.41%, mentre il DXY è stabile intorno a 98.79. Il prezzo del petrolio è sceso del 3.97% a $100.90, influenzando negativamente il sentiment.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and global economic uncertainty. The VIX is at 19.11, down 1.04%, but still above the 18 threshold. The S&P 500 declined by 0.41%, while the DXY is stable around 98.79. The oil price dropped by 3.97% to $100.90, negatively impacting sentiment.

market_impact_summary.it: I mercati azionari sono in calo, con l'S&P 500 che ha perso lo 0.41%. Il settore energetico è stato colpito dalla discesa del prezzo del petrolio del 3.97%. I tassi di interesse sono in aumento, con il US 10Y Yield che raggiunge il 4.32%. La liquidità globale, misurata dal Global M2, è in espansione del 4.9% su base annua.
market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets are down, with the S&P 500 losing 0.41%. The energy sector was hit by the 3.97% decline in oil prices. Interest rates are rising, with the US 10Y Yield reaching 4.32%. Global liquidity, measured by Global M2, is expanding at 4.9% year-over-year.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.97%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.33%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura mista per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di ieri, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in calo dello 0.41%, il VIX è sceso dell'1.04% sotto quota 20. L'oro si mantiene sopra i 4700 dollari l'oncia, mentre il petrolio è sceso del 3.97% sotto i 101 dollari. Il DXY è in calo dello 0.01%.

La situazione in Medio Oriente resta tesa, con possibili implicazioni per i mercati. La Banca del Giappone ha posticipato la decisione sui tassi a causa dell'incertezza.

Oggi si attendono dati macro importanti, tra cui il PIL degli USA e l'inflazione dell'Eurozona. La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi fermi al 2.00% per i depositi.

audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

Asian markets closed mixed. The Nikkei gained 0.97% to 59,716, while the Shanghai Composite dropped 0.33% to 4,079.90. This sets a cautious tone for European and US markets.

In Western markets, the S&P 500 fell 0.41% to 7,108.40. The VIX dropped 1.04% to 19.11, still below 20. The Dollar Index edged down 0.01% to 98.79. Gold holds above $4,700/oz, down 0.04% to $4,703.00/oz. Oil prices plunged, with Brent crude down 3.97% to $100.90. The STOXX 600 declined 0.72% to 60.75.

Geopolitical tensions are high, with the Bank of Japan postponing its April rate hike amid Iran uncertainty. The US Federal Reserve's rate stance and global economic data will be closely watched. No major economic data releases are scheduled for today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin is holding steady around seventy-seven thousand eight hundred seventy dollars, with no significant change, up zero point zero zero percent. Meanwhile, ETF inflows are positive, with two hundred twenty-three point three million dollars flowing in.

In the altcoin space, Ethereum is down zero point nine one percent to two thousand three hundred eighteen dollars, Solana is down zero point one nine percent to eighty-five point four nine dollars, and Binance Coin is up zero point four one percent to six hundred thirty-seven point eight seven dollars.

The Fear & Greed Index is at thirty-nine, classified as Fear. Overall sentiment remains cautious as investors monitor market developments and regulatory news.

Thanks for tuning in and we'll see you tomorrow. Have a great day and goodbye from Price Alert.

articles.title: Amid wartime disruptions, most emerging-market central banks will follow the Fed
articles.snippet: A main takeaway from last week's spring meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank is that emerging-market and developing economies (EMs) will suffer more than high-income countries from the repercussions of the Iran war. articles.title: Cryptoasset service providers as financial intermediaries: risks and policy approaches
articles.snippet: Cryptoasset service providers (CASPs) have expanded well beyond their initial roles as trading platforms and custodial service providers. The largest firms now offer a broad range of products, including yield/earn programmes, margin and secured lending, derivatives and token issuance. Some of these products closely resemble financial intermediation activities traditionally performed by banks and prime brokers. As such, many institutions can be better described as multifunction cryptoasset intermediaries (MCIs). When MCIs accept customer cryptoassets through investment programmes and use those assets to fund lending, market making and other activities, they take on credit, liquidity and maturity risk. Members of the UK House of Lords International Relations and Defence Committee attended Chatham House on 22 April to launch their new report, ‘ Adjusting to the new realities: Rebalancing the UK–US relationship ’. Lord Robertson, Chair of the committee, described the strains on UK–US relations brought about by President Donald Trump’s tariffs, threats to seize Greenland, and decision not to consult the UK before launching the war on Iran, highlighting a ‘growing divergence between Westminster and Washington’. articles.title: Airwaves of Power: Why the Pentagon Should Shift to a Commercial-First Spectrum Model
articles.snippet: The U.S. military is firing million-dollar missiles at Iranian drones that cost a tiny fraction as much — a striking example of the kind of overmatch modern warfare punishes.The Department of Defense’s approach to electromagnetic spectrum policy follows a similar logic, occupying prime mid-band frequencies for vital but relatively low-throughput national security uses — including radars, satellite communications, navigation, and electronic warfare — even as those same bands could generate much larger commercial, allied, and strategic returns.The Pentagon understandably views spectrum through a national security lens, but the current allocation reflects less strategic optimization than a legacy of policy choices The post Airwaves of Power: Why the Pentagon Should Shift to a Commercial-First

articles.title: Policymakers vs. the Iran War Shock
articles.snippet: Because markets, central banks, and governments move at different speeds—and sometimes in different directions—mistimed policy responses to major shocks can exacerbate, rather than mitigate, the depth and duration of a crisis. Fortunately, if this major lesson from the 1970s is heeded, the risk can be managed.

articles.title: A Formal Defense Pact in the Indo-Pacific Is the Wrong Answer
articles.snippet: The debate over how best to deter China in the western Pacific has reached a new level of ambition. Ely Ratner, a former senior defense official in the Biden administration, proposed a “Pacific Defense Pact” — a legally binding multilateral treaty among the United States, Japan, Australia, and the Philippines. This reflects serious concerns over China’s rise and its potential future use of force along the first island chain. The underlying diagnosis is sound: Existing U.S. alliances in the region lack an integrated command and control structure and the collective responsiveness required to credibly deter China in a high-intensity conflict. The post A Formal Defense Pact in the Indo-Pacific Is the Wrong Answer appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Electrification Is the Real Energy Hedge—and China Knows It
articles.snippet: Every time oil prices rise, Europe falls into the same familiar cycle. Politicians promise relief, analysts debate OPEC strategy, governments consider subsidies, and consumers prepare for higher transport and heating costs. It is a ritual of crisis management that assumes one thing above all else: oil will remain central, and Europe’s role is simply to cope with the consequences. China is taking a different approach. Rather than endlessly managing fossil-fuel volatility, it is steadily reducing how much oil matters to its economy. That is…
